why: Shorter, concrete three-question frame, ends on a clear action for the student.
Cuts narrated backstory and the declared 'anxiety'; keeps the claim and the action.
Guess prompt comes before the answer is revealed, so the prediction is real.
Drops the abstract 'shape the rules together' filler line; shorter.
Adds the concrete mismatch consequence, which completes the spot-check act.
'Session' is the established unit, while 'run' is vaguer.
The title states the claim itself, and the closer is trimmed.
Drops the parenthetical recap of M6 and is shorter.
Cuts the restating tail clause; fewer words.
Cuts the closing moralising sentence.
'Exercise' is the accurate term for what was run; the two versions are otherwise the same.
The 'no pre-made prompt' line is shorter, and the scrollback reference is clear.
Drops the forward hint to Module 4 and the 'that list is the lesson' closer; B is shorter and states the practice plainly.
'The training runs on YOUR real work' is a neutral statement; A's 'YOUR real work is the material' is the more abrupt phrasing, and B reads more smoothly.
Cuts the filler sentence 'The move is the same every time' and goes straight to the action.
Removes the forward-hint closer about Phases 3 and 4, per the rule to cut forward hints.
Drops the narrated restatement of what the agent does, which is shorter and keeps the student's judging role in focus.
'It often isn't' reads as plain and direct, while B's 'often just' adds a mild dismissive tone; the two are otherwise near identical.
B adds a sentence telling students they are not learning the strands yet, which is a restatement and a hedge; A is shorter.
A's 'Watch the tool list come back rather than typing along' is an extra instruction; B is a simple, active 'Ask these one at a time'.
'Three new concerns' matches the three bullets and is more concrete, though the 'wall' metaphor is in both.
'Three pressures' gives a concrete, picturable count that matches the three bullets.
'Where the file gets read' is a plain orienting title; A's 'Three agents using the file' is vaguer.
Names a concrete, current thing to look at (how MCP-connector tools land in the same set), which is more specific and useful than the vague 'what it leaves out'.
A's added closer 'Three modules in, this is your practice now' is a declarative restatement and a narrator-style claim; B is shorter.
A cuts sentences and is tighter and more concrete; B's em-dash explanatory asides add length.
B drops the redundant 'This is your side-quest lane' framing, which is a loaded, made-up concept, so it is shorter and more neutral.
A's added opener 'A strong candidate for a team PR' is a fragment that restates the title, so B is shorter and cleaner.
'Check what Claude proposes' is the precise verb; 'Read' would imply reading all of it.
B states a concrete claim, while A's 'see the forest before the trees' is an idiom and a witty closer.
B's title is the actionable claim and shorter, and A's title is more abstract.
B's title is an action the student can take tomorrow, while A's is a loaded one-liner.
B tells students to ask Claude to set up the status line, which fits the rule on tool features, and it is clearer.
'Decision, written as an ADR' is concrete and the acronym is expanded, while A's 'a future engineer can inspect' is vaguer.
A drops the made-up concept 'the wall', and the rules say to cut those.
B's title is concrete and pictureable, and A's 'how agentic knowledge compounds' is an abstract claim.
Shorter header; 'context' is redundant with 'window' for this audience.
Cuts the closer and restatement; neutral register.
Header 'Things a good plan has' avoids a count that must match the list; fewer words.
Concrete instruction to ask Claude; A's 'Spot what's still generic' is an imperative with no object and leaves the student passive about how.
The closing line prevents misreading the phases as a sequence and carries a real concept; one sentence, accurate.
Permission framing ('you don't need to get it right first time') lands the experiment idea and lowers the stakes.
Concrete action the student can take, plain and short; A is abstract and hedged.
Cuts connective narration and forward hints; just the list.
Avoids 'committed change' git jargon and plain 'alternative' is clearer; drops the extra 'gives you the floor' sentence.
